description.en: Trajecto is a modular ontology for semantic trajectories: GPS-derived movement of people, the points of interest they interact with, the patterns, purposes and contexts of that movement, and the user profiles learned from it. The core module defines the moving person, entities of interest and interactions, and reuses the datAcron trajectory model (Trajectory, TrajectoryPart, RawPosition, MovingObject) and DUL. It imports the other eleven modules and the purpose concept scheme, and is the entry point to the whole ontology.

publisher.value: i-Lab, Department of Cultural Technology and Communication, University of the Aegean

bibliographicCitation.value: Angelis, S. (2026). Semantic Trajectory Analytics and Recommender Systems: Engineering Semantic Trajectories as Knowledge Graphs. Doctoral dissertation, University of the Aegean.

comment.en: The specific spatial point that the recording activity aims to record. The point of interest may be literally one geometric point or an central point of a wider entity of interest.
Deprecated: use patterns:ImmersiveMovement.
The specific event that the recording activity aims to record. This event may be a natural phenomenon, the movement of an individual etc.
Deprecated: use patterns:CasualMovement.
Deprecated since 1.1.0: renamed to RegionOfInterest.
The reason a trajectory is undertaken. The purpose module specializes it; trajectories point to purpose concepts through hasPurpose.
Deprecated: use patterns:ExploratoryMovement.
Engagement level of a trajectory with a moderate share of meaningful interactions.
Engagement level of a trajectory with a high share of meaningful and immersive interactions.
Engagement level of a trajectory with few or no meaningful interactions.

Engagement of a trajectory as a whole, derived from the share of its meaningful and immersive interactions. Values: HighEngagement, MediumEngagement, LowEngagement. The temporal-dwell module models engagement of single dwell events separately.
An event of interest of a cultural nature, such as a festival or an exhibition opening.
A person whose movement is recorded as one or more trajectories.
The entity of interest of any kind (object, event, living organism), that the recording activity aims to record.
A POI in the top quintile of betweenness: it bridges otherwise separate parts of the flow graph.
A POI with none of the other structural roles.
A POI in the top quintile of both co-visitation degree and PageRank.
A POI with clearly more outgoing than incoming flow.
A high-PageRank POI with clearly more incoming than outgoing flow.
Structural role of a POI in the graphs of co-visitation and flow between POIs, derived from its degree, betweenness and PageRank relative to the other POIs.
Deprecated: use patterns:TargetedSegment.
A raw position that belongs to a stop.
A trajectory part during which the moving object stays within a small area for a minimum time.
The region that a recording activity aims to record, such as a forest, an archaeological site or a town.
The means by which a trajectory part is travelled, such as walking, cycling or bus.
The specific physical object that the recording activity aims to record. The object of interest may be a tree, a monument, a person etc.
An interaction between moving persons within an area of interest.

Deprecated: navigation styles are modeled as movement patterns in the patterns module (patterns:TargetedSegment, patterns:CasualMovement, patterns:ExploratoryMovement, patterns:ImmersiveMovement) and asserted with patterns:exhibitsPattern.
Deprecated since 1.1.0: renamed to Stop.
Something a moving entity does with, or near, an entity of interest during a trajectory. Specialized as POI interactions in the POI module.
A scored similarity between two trajectories along one facet, such as shared POI categories, navigation pattern, temporal context or purpose.
Jaccard similarity of the POI categories two trajectories interact with.
Relates a trajectory part to a point of interest associated with it.
The other trajectory of a trajectory similarity.
Two trajectories share a purpose.
Number of meaningful interactions of a trajectory.
Correlates an entity of interest with the type of interest that it presents.
Relates a trajectory to a segment that is part of it.
Northing (y) of a position in a projected or indoor coordinate reference system, in meters. Used instead of longitude where positions are planar.
Two trajectories share a navigation pattern.
Specifies the moving object which forms a trajectory
Relates a trajectory cluster to a trajectory it groups.
Identifier of the co-visitation community a POI belongs to.
Floor number of a position, for indoor positioning.
Inverse of hasNextPosition: relates a raw position to an earlier position of the same trajectory.

Relates a trajectory to the POI interactions that occur at its positions. A shortcut for the chain from a trajectory to its positions to their interactions, so that classes over interactions can be defined on trajectories.
External identifier of a region of interest, such as an OpenStreetMap or geocoder place ID.
Postal address of a region of interest.
Easting (x) of a position in a projected or indoor coordinate reference system, in meters. Used instead of latitude where positions are planar, for example in indoor tracking.
Zero-based order of a raw position within its trajectory.
Betweenness centrality of a POI in the POI flow graph.
Number of distinct POIs a trajectory interacts with.
Relates a raw position to a POI interaction that takes place at it.
Jaccard similarity of the temporal contexts of two trajectories.
The OpenStreetMap tag (key=value) that identifies the type of an entity of interest.
Deprecated: use patterns:exhibitsPattern.
Deprecated since 1.1.0: renamed to happensDuringEventOfInterest.
Inverse of formsTrajectory: relates a trajectory to the moving object that forms it.
Inverse of datAcron:hasWeatherCondition.
Number of immersive interactions of a trajectory.
Deprecated duplicate of isTrajectoryFormedBy: relates a trajectory to its moving object.
Relates a POI to its structural role.
Number of distinct POI categories a trajectory interacts with.
Description of the Wikidata entity a POI is linked to.
PageRank of a POI in the POI flow graph.
Velocity value attached to a geometry, as recorded by the source.
Links a trajectory to a behavioral event detected within its position sequence.
Relates a trajectory part to a region of interest it passes through.
Relates a trajectory to its purpose, a concept of the purpose concept scheme.
Sum of the dwell times of the interactions of a trajectory, in seconds.
Label of the Wikidata entity a POI is linked to.
Deprecated duplicate of formsTrajectory: relates a moving object to a trajectory it forms.
Relates a raw position to a later position of the same trajectory. Asserted between consecutive positions; as the property is transitive, a reasoner extends it to every later position.
Relates a trajectory part to the mode of transportation used for it.
Relates an agent to an interaction it takes part in.
Relates a trajectory part to a stop it comprises.
Correlates an entity of interest with the type of interest that it presents.
Relates a trajectory part to an event of interest that takes place while it is recorded.
Recording time of a raw position, as an ISO 8601 local date-time string.
Score of a trajectory similarity, from 0 to 1.
Relates a trajectory part to an event that occurred during it.
Relates a trajectory to its engagement level. The engagement classes of the profiles module are defined over it.
